q: Why are water supply pipes resized in high-rise buildings?
o: To handle the pressure difference between the service and the fixtures
n: In high-rise buildings static pressure varies greatly with height, so supply pipes are resized and zoned to handle the pressure difference between the service and the fixtures. Source: ASPE Plumbing Engineering Design Handbook (high-rise water supply).

q: What principle governs the sizing of pipes in plumbing system design?
o: The smaller the pipes, the higher the pressure
The pressure is the same regardless of pipe size
The bigger the pipe, the higher the pressure; the smaller the pipe, the lower the pressure
The pressure of pipes depends only on the material used
n: For the same flow, a smaller pipe gives higher velocity and the outlet jet has more force. Pipes are sized from the required flow and pressure (friction loss rises as the pipe gets smaller). Source: ASPE Plumbing Engineering Design Handbook; fluid mechanics.

q: Where is water pressure highest in a plumbing system?
n: Static water pressure rises with depth below the source, so it is highest at the lowest fixture. Source: Fluid statics; ASPE Plumbing Engineering Design Handbook.

q: What mainly affects water pipe sizing in a multi-story building?
n: In multi-story buildings, building height (static head) and the pressure needed at the highest fixtures mainly govern pipe sizing and zoning. Source: ASPE Plumbing Engineering Design Handbook.

q: What is the main reason for increasing pipe size in a supply system?
n: Pipe size is increased mainly to carry a larger flow at acceptable velocity and friction loss. Source: ASPE Plumbing Engineering Design Handbook.

q: Which part of Metro Manila does Manila Water serve?
n: Manila Water holds the East Zone concession of Metro Manila. Source: MWSS concession agreements; Manila Water company website.

q: Which part of Metro Manila does Maynilad serve?
n: Maynilad Water Services holds the West Zone concession of Metro Manila. Source: MWSS concession agreements; Maynilad company website.

q: Which material is NOT recommended for rooftop water tanks?
n: Galvanized steel tanks lose their zinc coating, then rust and taint stored water. Stainless steel, fiberglass and polyethylene tanks do not corrode. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (water storage tanks); ASPE Plumbing Engineering Design Handbook.

q: What is the minimum number of floors that requires an Elevated Water Tank (EWT)?
n: Elevated water tanks become necessary in tall buildings (about 10 floors and up), where gravity storage on the roof supplies upper floors more reliably than pumping alone. Source: ASPE Plumbing Engineering Design Handbook (high-rise water supply).

q: What is the minimum distance between a water well and a sewer line or septic tank?
n: A water well must be at least 15.2 m (50 ft) from a sewer line, septic tank or other source of contamination. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (location of wells); DOH Code on Sanitation (PD 856).

q: Which valve is suitable for embedding in soil?
n: A ball valve is compact, quarter-turn and sealed, so it suits buried (embedded) service with a valve box. Source: AWWA C507 (ball valves); ASPE Plumbing Engineering Design Handbook.

q: Which of these valves is NOT meant for regulating flow?
n: Gate valves are for full open or full closed only. Partly open, the gate vibrates and wears. Diaphragm, globe and needle valves are made to regulate. Source: ASPE Plumbing Engineering Design Handbook (valve selection).

q: Which linear-motion valve is used to regulate water flow?
n: A globe valve has a linear-motion stem that lifts a disc off its seat, so it regulates flow. Ball and butterfly valves are quarter-turn and check valves are automatic. Source: MSS SP-80; ASPE Plumbing Engineering Design Handbook.

q: Which of the following valves is best for water containing solid waste?
n: A gate valve gives a straight, unobstructed full-bore passage when open, so water carrying solids passes without clogging the valve. Source: ASPE Plumbing Engineering Design Handbook (valve selection).

q: What is the minimum required slope for a water supply pipe?
n: Pressurized water supply pipes need no minimum slope, since flow is driven by pressure. Slope is required for gravity drainage. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines.

q: How are HDPE pipes joined?
n: HDPE pipes are joined by heat fusion, commonly electrofusion fittings or butt fusion. Source: ASTM F1055; ASTM F2620.

q: How are PPR pipes joined?
n: PPR pipes are joined by socket (heat) fusion: pipe and fitting are heated on a tool and pushed together to fuse. Source: DIN 16962; PPR manufacturer installation guides.

q: How are PVC pipes joined?
n: PVC pipes are joined with solvent cement (after primer), which chemically fuses the pipe and socket. Source: ASTM D2855 (solvent-cemented joints).

q: How are hubless cast iron pipes joined?
o: Neoprene couplings with stainless band clamps
n: Hubless cast iron pipes are joined with neoprene sleeve couplings and stainless steel band clamps. Source: CISPI 310.

q: What is used to join Concrete pipes?
n: Concrete pipes are traditionally joined with cement mortar packed into the bell-and-spigot joint. Rubber gasket joints are a modern option. Source: ASTM C14 (concrete sewer pipe); National Plumbing Code of the Philippines.

q: Which flexible plastic tubing is suitable for hot and cold pressure lines and resists acids and alkalis but not fuel oil, gasoline or kerosene?
n: Polybutylene (PB) tubing is flexible and rated for hot and cold pressure lines and resists acids and alkalis, but is attacked by petroleum products such as fuel oil, gasoline and kerosene. Source: Plumbing materials references (ASTM D3309, polybutylene tubing).

q: What is the minimum size of the supply pipe distributing the main line to the primary branch?
n: The supply pipe from the main to the primary branch is sized at a minimum of about 50 mm (2 in.) in standard design tables. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (water supply sizing).

q: Which practice is illegal?
o: Providing a cistern to supply the building
Feeding each building's cistern from the main
Using a booster pump to draw water straight from the main
n: Pumping directly from the public main with a booster pump is illegal: it draws down pressure for neighbors and risks backflow contamination. Buildings must pump from their own cistern. Source: MWSS/water utility regulations; National Plumbing Code of the Philippines.

q: In a three-storey residential building, where is the water pressure the highest?
n: Static pressure increases with depth, so in a three-storey building it is highest in the underground (lowest) piping. Source: Fluid statics; ASPE Plumbing Engineering Design Handbook.

q: What valve is typically installed where the service line enters, to shut off the whole building?
n: A full-port gate valve is installed where the service line enters, as the main shut-off for the whole building. Source: National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (building supply shutoff).

q: What is the greenish film that forms on copper over time?
n: Copper weathers to a greenish patina (basic copper carbonates and sulfates) that protects the metal underneath. Source: Copper Development Association.

q: Which hand tool is used to flare tubing?
n: A flaring tool spreads the end of soft copper or other tubing into a cone, so it seals in a flare fitting. Source: Copper Development Association, Copper Tube Handbook.

q: Which valve gives the finest flow control?
n: A needle valve has a long tapered needle in a small seat, giving the finest control of small flows. Source: ASPE Plumbing Engineering Design Handbook; valve manufacturer literature.

q: What tool removes burrs inside a cut pipe?
n: A reamer removes the burr left inside a cut pipe, restoring the full bore so flow is not restricted. Source: Copper Development Association, Copper Tube Handbook.

q: What valve at a tank outlet or pump suction prevents backflow?
n: A foot valve is a check valve with a strainer at the bottom of a pump suction line. It keeps the pipe primed by preventing backflow to the tank. Source: Hydraulic Institute; ASPE Plumbing Engineering Design Handbook.
